item.title: Update: BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day: Rapid7 reports a Metasploit module; the actor's persistence survives reset
item.description: Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis of CVE-2026-102764 on 2026-10-30 and says a Metasploit module now implements the unauthenticated file-write to code-execution chain; its successful request is an extensionless URL that rules matching only .php requests miss.
item.content:encoded:
Update31 Oct 2026 03:39 UTCrun 2026-10-31T0256Z-intelheadlinesummaryimmediate_actionsourcesevidenceactionsbody

Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis of CVE-2026-102764 on 2026-10-30 and says a Metasploit module now implements the unauthenticated file-write to code-execution chain; its successful request is an extensionless URL that rules matching only .php requests miss.

Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis on 2026-10-30 and says a Metasploit module now implements the chain, with PHP and Unix Command targets (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). An anonymous customer session, started through the public customer connection, sends a message whose source address carries a reserved local router ID; the appliance's customer worker accepts that address as proof that the request came from a local component, which exposes an internal file-transfer service with its native filesystem provider. Rapid7 used it to write a PHP file into the site's public directory and ran it as the site's operating-system user (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). The successful request was an extensionless URL, because the web server answers a direct .php request with 404 and maps an extensionless URL to the existing file, so detection that only searches for requests ending in .php would miss it; the appliance's thin-scc logs record file-transfer stream creation and rejected requests (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). Rapid7 tested Remote Support 24.1.2 and says other affected releases and fixed builds have not been established; BeyondTrust's advisory remains the reference for affected and fixed versions (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).

Open finding: CVE-2026-102764, BeyondTrust Remote Support: an unauthenticated file-operation flaw exploited as a zero-day since late August by a suspected China-nexus actor that left a web shell and boot-time sudo persistence (CVSS 4.0 9.3) →

item.title: privatim cloud guidance v3.02: public bodies keep their own keys for sensitive data; big-vendor SaaS mostly out
item.description: privatim, the conference of the Swiss data-protection authorities, revised its guidance on cloud-specific risks for public bodies on 2026-10-02 (version 3.02, replacing the version of 3 February 2022). For particularly sensitive personal data the public body must encrypt with keys only it can use, outsourcing such data or data under a statutory duty of confidentiality to standard SaaS from large international providers is in most cases inadmissible, and the body's top management is to confirm the residual risk in writing.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOA2

privatim revises its cloud guidance for Swiss public bodies (Merkblatt v3.02, 2 October 2026): sensitive data stays under the body's own keys, standard SaaS from Microsoft, Google, AWS and SAP is in most cases inadmissible for secrecy-bound data, and top management signs the residual risk

privatim, the conference of the Swiss data-protection authorities, dates version 3.02 of its guidance "Cloud-specific risks and measures" to 2 October 2026 (privatim, 2026-10-02); it replaces the version of 3 February 2022 (DCOD, 2026-10-27). For particularly sensitive personal data the public body must encrypt, the keys may be available only to it, and outsourcing such data, or data under a statutory duty of confidentiality, to SaaS from large international providers, with Microsoft, Google, AWS and SAP named, is in most cases inadmissible because of the untenable risk (privatim, 2026-10-02). Keys may stay with the provider only where no untenable risk follows and the provider is bound by contract to use them only with the body's express consent and to log every access (privatim, 2026-10-02).

The body, or its top management, is to confirm in writing that it has understood the risks and accepts the residual risk, and data the cloud services generate about their users, such as telemetry and logging data, is to be treated with the same care and contract terms as the content data (privatim, 2026-10-02). The five risk areas are contract design, places of processing including foreign authority access, confidentiality with encryption and key management, user data, and sub-processors (privatim, 2026-10-02).

Defender takeaway
The guidance addresses public bodies subject to Swiss data-protection law; a body that runs or plans standard SaaS from the named providers for sensitive or secrecy-bound data is advised to keep its own encryption keys, to have top management sign the residual risk, and to hold provider telemetry and logs about its users to the same contract terms.

item.title: Lumen: Volt Typhoon's Silent Train relay chains fronted zero-days against SD-WAN, N-central and KACE
item.description: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reports that Volt Typhoon ran exploitation, credential access and exfiltration through Silent Train, rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT and enterprise devices that it rebuilt for each operation, and that its monitoring uncovered one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against endpoint and network management platforms and SD-WAN orchestrators, among them Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, N-able N-central and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator. The reported victims are US-centred and the report names no Swiss or European victim.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

Silent Train: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs describes the rotating relay network Volt Typhoon used for one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against management and control-plane platforms (Quest KACE, Versa Director, N-able N-central, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator)

Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reports that Volt Typhoon used a covert framework it calls Silent Train, first seen in late 2023, for the phases that need protection: exploitation, credential access, data exfiltration and continued access to victims (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). A session starts from a virtual private server outside the US, passes through compromised non-US SOHO and IoT devices and leaves through a compromised US device before the victim; more than 27 device classes were enrolled, from TP-Link routers and Netgear Orbi devices to Fortinet appliances and CyberPanel servers, and the enterprise platforms stayed in chains for one to three months as final hops (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). The operators exploit exposed web interfaces on the relay devices and deploy only what chained SSH needs, namely temporary SSH services, keys, configuration files and living-off-the-land utilities, with reverse tunnels over open-source proxies in later variants; sessions averaged about four hours, and at the end the operators removed all artifacts and dismantled the chain (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28).

Lumen says its monitoring helped identify one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against endpoint and network management platforms and SD-WAN orchestrators: Quest KACE, where the activity looked like an undisclosed flaw, affected more than 30 victims and fell after Quest's October 2025 updates (a moderate-confidence assessment); Versa Director in 2024; the N-able N-central flaws CVE-2025-8875 and CVE-2025-8876; Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN through CVE-2026-20127, exploited by late 2025 and after Cisco's February 2026 disclosure; and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator through the zero-day later designated CVE-2026-16812 (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). Post-incident analysis found in-memory webshells, credential harvesting and abuse of native platform features such as endpoint control and remote file transfers, and in several cases erased or altered logs (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). The victims it names are US government, telecommunications, defence-industrial, managed-service and critical-infrastructure organisations, concentrated in Hawaii, California and Texas, and it names no European or Swiss victim (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). The Hacker News carries the same findings from a report Lumen shared with it (The Hacker News, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
Internet-reachable management and control-plane platforms (endpoint management, SD-WAN controllers and orchestrators, out-of-band administration), and edge devices with exposed web interfaces, which can be enrolled as relay hops without any data of the owner being the target.
Detection
Telemetry classes are administrative logins, API calls, remote file transfers and configuration changes on management platforms outside normal administration hours or workflow, in-memory web shells that leave no file on disk, and, on edge devices, temporary SSH services, unfamiliar keys and outbound reverse tunnels to unfamiliar upstream hosts (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28).
Defender takeaway
Restrict the administrative interfaces of management and control-plane platforms to a VPN, jump host or management network and prioritise their patching, as Lumen advises, and treat an edge device that shows temporary SSH services or reverse tunnels as a possible relay in someone else's intrusion chain.

item.title: CrowdStrike: VAPOR PANDA runs ARTEX against 200+ organisations, European foreign ministries among them
item.description: CrowdStrike reports that from 2026-10-17 the China-nexus actor VAPOR PANDA used the ARTEX agent framework, driven mainly by the DeepSeek model, against more than 200 organisations worldwide, with the controller CrowdStrike saw directing exploitation in at least 14 countries, including foreign ministries in Europe, a European country's presidency, prime minister's office and defence, justice, finance and intelligence entities, and a Greek government entity. CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation at nine organisations, with the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor loaded by a renamed legitimate binary, and says this campaign is separate from the Storm-0940 ARTEX activity Microsoft reported.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB3

VAPOR PANDA: CrowdStrike reports a China-nexus actor running the ARTEX agent framework against more than 200 organisations from 17 October, among them foreign ministries in Europe and a Greek government entity, and deploying the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor

CrowdStrike OverWatch reports that from 2026-10-17 a single ARTEX controller linked to VAPOR PANDA infrastructure directed exploitation against entities in at least 14 countries over 11 days, and that the campaign reached more than 200 organisations, including foreign ministries in Europe (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). One engagement focused on a single European country, its foreign ministry, presidency, prime minister's office and defence, justice, finance and intelligence entities, and another targeted 19 US organisations in pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, defence, nuclear and finance (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation at nine organisations and password spraying and credential scanning against at least 12 more, among them government entities in Europe (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). CrowdStrike states that the campaign is separate from the Storm-0940 ARTEX activity Microsoft reported and is VAPOR PANDA's first observed use of AI-driven tooling (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).

The framework ran mainly on the DeepSeek model, with a human operator steering the agents at decision points while they pursued web, cloud, container, Active Directory, mail and VPN paths in parallel (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). In transcripts at a US pharmaceutical company the agent chained an unsigned SAML assertion with an XML external entity flaw to query the cloud instance metadata service and obtain a role that could issue administration commands to thousands of instances; at a second it deployed web shells, abused an unauthenticated orchestration service for root in a container environment, read LAPS passwords and abused resource-based constrained delegation (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). Against a Greek government entity the operator supplied a 2022 directory export from the mail server whose authentication keys had likely not been rotated; the agent forged an administrator token, read mailboxes and used VPN configurations from a user's sent mail, with a VPN client key the operator described as coming from a May 2024 email leak, to reach the internal network (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). The operator also told the agents to find domain Windows hosts without the CrowdStrike Falcon sensor (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). At a Middle East interior ministry and a Latin American foreign ministry the actor loaded the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor through a legitimate GameHook binary renamed svchost.exe that loads a malicious DLL (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). No Swiss target is named.

Exposure
Government, mail, identity and VPN estates where a directory export or backup holding authentication keys has never been rotated, SAML service providers that accept unsigned assertions, and cloud instances that still allow instance metadata service version 1; CrowdStrike names foreign ministries and government entities in Europe among the targets.
Detection
Telemetry classes are authentication logs (password spraying and credential scanning against many accounts, an administrator token minted outside the identity provider, VPN logins that use a configuration or key from an old mailbox or leak), cloud control-plane audit (administration commands issued to many instances through the cloud systems manager, instance metadata queries from an application), process lineage (a legitimate GameHook binary renamed svchost.exe loading a malicious DLL) and endpoint inventory queries for hosts without the security agent; CrowdStrike lists ARTEX-named command-line parameters, cloud roles and a directory under ProgramData as hunt markers (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).
Defender takeaway
Rotate keys held in old directory exports and backups, require signed SAML assertions and IMDSv2, and hunt authentication and cloud audit logs for the parallel, many-target pattern an operator-steered agent produces; CrowdStrike expects China-nexus actors to keep adopting agent frameworks.

item.title: Talos IR Q3: public administration tied for most targeted; vishing into RMM and EDR killing mark the ransomware cases
item.description: Cisco Talos Incident Response's Q3 2026 trends report names public administration, tied with finance at 18 percent of engagements, as the most targeted sector, and puts phishing first and public-facing application exploitation second among initial-access techniques. Its ransomware cases (27 percent of engagements) show help-desk vishing that leads the victim to allow remote access through a legitimate remote-management tool, and operators who uninstall or terminate EDR, including with vulnerable drivers.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOB2

ANNUAL REPORT: Cisco Talos Incident Response trends Q3 2026: public administration tied with finance as the most targeted sector, help-desk vishing into remote-management tools, and ransomware operators uninstalling and killing EDR

Cisco Talos Incident Response reports that in Q3 2026 financial organisations made up 18 percent of its engagements, tying with public administration as the most targeted sector (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Phishing was the leading initial-access technique at 37 percent of engagements and exploitation of public-facing applications second at 33 percent; the phishing cases include numerous actors who phone the victim as the IT help desk to get remote access allowed through a legitimate remote monitoring and management (RMM) tool (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Ransomware and pre-ransomware cases were 27 percent of engagements, with The Gentlemen, Qilin, Rhysida and the closed group Interlock among the families and a new variant, VYPR, that Talos calls operationally immature: it had no leak site when seen, reused leaked Conti-derived source code and exfiltrated over several days (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29).

The VYPR intrusion began with a vishing call that had the user start a Microsoft Quick Assist session; the actor then used RMM software that ran PowerShell to download and install an MSI from a remote address, with MeshAgent, Rclone, PsExec, an IP scanner and mstsc as tools, and disabled EDR with several vulnerable drivers (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Interlock operators repeatedly tried to uninstall Cisco Secure Endpoint, used PsExec and taskkill to end security services and integrity checkers, turned off Windows Defender real-time protection and cleared event logs (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Talos names insufficient logging (over 40 percent of engagements), weak credential and secret handling, and absent or incomplete MFA as the most common weaknesses, and recommends centralised logging with at least 90 days of retention (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29).

Exposure
An organisation whose help desk or staff can be reached by phone and whose endpoints permit Quick Assist or an unapproved RMM agent; Talos names public administration among the most targeted sectors in its caseload.
Detection
In process-creation and software-install telemetry, an RMM or Quick Assist session started after an inbound call, followed by PowerShell run under the RMM agent that downloads an installer from an external address; in endpoint and service-control telemetry, attempts to uninstall the EDR agent, PsExec or taskkill ending security services, Defender real-time protection switched off, vulnerable kernel drivers loaded, and event logs cleared.
Defender takeaway
Treat a remote-support session that nobody at the help desk started as the vishing signal and inventory which RMM tools and Quick Assist are permitted on endpoints; alert on EDR uninstall and security-service termination as a ransomware precursor; and centralise logs with the 90-day minimum retention Talos recommends, because actors delete logs on the endpoint.

item.description: CISA added the ESX insufficient-logging flaw CVE-2026-41709 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28, and CrowdStrike says the actor WARP PANDA exploited it as a zero-day in vCenter-environment intrusions as late as early 2026; Broadcom's advisory still carries no exploitation statement. The CVE record moves to exploited and KEV-listed, and ESX audit logs can no longer be treated as a complete record of administrator activity.
item.content:encoded:
Update29 Oct 2026 04:53 UTCrun 2026-10-29T0255Z-intelsummaryupdated_atentitiestagstechniquescvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

CISA added the ESX insufficient-logging flaw CVE-2026-41709 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28, and CrowdStrike says the actor WARP PANDA exploited it as a zero-day in vCenter-environment intrusions as late as early 2026; Broadcom's advisory still carries no exploitation statement. The CVE record moves to exploited and KEV-listed, and ESX audit logs can no longer be treated as a complete record of administrator activity.

CISA added CVE-2026-41709, the ESX insufficient-logging flaw, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 on evidence of active exploitation, naming no actor (CISA KEV). CrowdStrike says WARP PANDA deployed several forms of malware in victims' VMware vCenter environments and that in several of these cases, as late as early 2026, the adversary exploited the ESXi command logging bypass CVE-2026-41709 as a zero-day; it describes intrusions at U.S.-based entities that included the legal sector, and gives no indicators, no account of what goes unlogged and no date of first exploitation (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-28). Broadcom's advisory rates the flaw 2.7 and carries no exploitation statement (Broadcom, 2026-07-29). CrowdStrike does not say how the actor obtained administrator rights on the host or whether the flaws of CVE-2026-59309 and CVE-2026-59310 were involved, so no link to them is drawn. Until the fix is installed, ESX logs from a period of administrator access are not reliable evidence of what was done; vCenter task and event records and syslog forwarded off the host are the sources to review.

item.title: Machelen municipality: foothold from a website's misleading instructions, 22 days to detection; Rhysida lists its files
item.description: The Belgian municipality of Machelen published a timeline in which attackers gained access to an internal laptop through misleading instructions on an external website on 2026-08-20, reached a user with high privileges on 2026-09-10 and were found on 2026-09-11; it confirms that personal data was stolen. Ransomware.live recorded on 2026-10-27 that the Rhysida group had listed the municipal and social-welfare file servers on its leak site, a claim the municipality has not confirmed.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOA2

Machelen (Belgium) municipality: its own timeline shows a foothold through misleading instructions on an external website on 2026-08-20, found 22 days later after a high-privilege user was reached, with personal data confirmed stolen and Rhysida now listing municipal and social-welfare files

Machelen's own timeline records that on 2026-08-20 attackers gained access to an internal laptop through misleading instructions on an external website, explored it extensively from 24 August to 1 September, and on 10 September had access to a user with high access rights and other IT systems; the municipality found the incident on 11 September, isolated all systems, reported to the Belgian CCB-CERT, restarted part of its systems from a backup of a safe date on 14 September and recorded the first evidence of leaked data on 17 September (Municipality of Machelen, 2026-09-22). It confirms that personal data was leaked and says the scope is still being investigated (Municipality of Machelen, 2026-09-22); the mayor had said on 14 September that no personal data appeared to be affected, and ITdaily reports that this proved wrong (ITdaily, 2026-09-23). Ransomware.live recorded on 2026-10-27 that Rhysida listed Machelen on its leak site, describing the listing as municipal and social-welfare file servers of about 1.3 million files, with client files that include passports and identity cards, nursing-home medical files and civil-status records, which are the group's own claims (Ransomware.live, 2026-10-27).

Detection
The timeline puts 22 days between first access and detection, with the first laptop explored from 24 August to 1 September; it names neither the website nor the commands, so the telemetry to review includes endpoint process creation after a user followed instructions on a web page and later use of a high-privilege account from that workstation, which is an inference from the timeline.
Defender takeaway
Treat a user who followed instructions from a website on a work laptop as a possible intrusion that can sit unseen for weeks; review high-privilege account activity from the user's workstation for the weeks after the event, not only the day it is reported.

item.title: Moldova: unauthenticated e-government services queried for about one million ID numbers; data on 750,000 extracted
item.description: Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency says that between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-23 attackers exploited flaws in state digital services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and, on preliminary estimates, extract data sets for about 750,000 of them, then used what they obtained to extract more from interconnected systems. The Prime Minister says foreign state involvement is being investigated and that AI allegedly helped find the flaws; Moldova has not attributed the attack, and the agency took 82 services under review and disconnected exposed services and more than 30 systems.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOA2

Moldova's government digital services: attackers used flaws in services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and extract data on about 750,000 of them between 19 and 23 October, and the Prime Minister says AI allegedly helped find the flaws

Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency (AGE) reported on 2026-10-27 that between 19 and 23 October attackers queried about one million national identification numbers (IDNPs) through state digital services and that, on preliminary estimates, data sets for about 750,000 of them were extracted; MOLDPRES had put the access requests at about 11 million on 2026-10-24 (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27; MOLDPRES, 2026-10-24). AGE's technical explanation is that the attackers exploited vulnerabilities in services reachable without authentication and then used the data they obtained for further extractions; the first attacks hit an electronic service that logged the legal basis of processing incorrectly, which is why citizens saw entries for civil-status document requests and driving-licence issue in the data-access history of the EVO app (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27). Data that may be affected, not every category for every person, includes name, date and place of birth, first-degree relatives, insured status, family doctor, social benefits, pensions, disability, driving licence, photograph, vehicles and companies owned or run, IBAN, tax debts and payment history; AGE says card data is not held on the platform and it found no unauthorised change to state registers (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27).

AGE stopped the extraction on 23 October at 11:30, reviewed 82 digital services and suspended the exposed ones, and its timeline says 82 public services and more than 30 information systems and administration panels were disconnected as a precaution on 23 October; it blocked further attempts on 25 and 27 October, and the Prime Minister's account is that 30 of the 82 services were disconnected (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27; MOLDPRES, 2026-10-28). The Prime Minister says the incident is not isolated, that foreign state actors are being investigated and that the attackers automated the extraction, with the use of artificial intelligence allegedly facilitating the identification and exploitation of the vulnerabilities (MOLDPRES, 2026-10-28). Moldova has not attributed the attack to any country or group (The Record, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
A public e-service of a federal, cantonal or communal administration that returns person data for an identifier without authentication, or whose output feeds other registers, since AGE says the extraction chained from unauthenticated services into further data (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27).
Detection
Citizens noticed the abuse because the data-access history in the EVO app showed processing for civil-status document requests and driving-licence issue that they had not made, so a data-subject-visible access log is a detection channel (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27). On the server side the relevant telemetry is per-service request volume and sequential or bulk identifier lookups from one source; the sources give no breakdown of the request pattern, so that is an inference from about 11 million requests against about one million numbers.
Defender takeaway
List the public services that answer for a person identifier without authentication and check what each one returns, whether it feeds other registers and whether its access log records the true purpose; rate limits and alerts on bulk lookups belong in front of every such service.

item.title: Inside IT: SafePay published about 49 GB from a Bernese wastewater association; the association declines to comment
item.description: SafePay claimed an attack on the Bernese wastewater-treatment association ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal on 2026-09-15, and Inside IT reports of 2026-10-27 that the group has now put about 49 GB of stolen data into the darknet. Risikomonitor's analysis, which Inside IT relays and which is not verified independently, finds data on more than 1,200 identifiable persons, bank statements, 255 password hits in files and a third party's monitoring-portal credentials stored on the association's server; the association will not comment, and no source says how the attackers got in.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOC3

ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal (canton Bern, communal wastewater-treatment association): SafePay has put about 49 GB into the darknet, which Risikomonitor's analysis, relayed by Inside IT, finds holds personal records, bank statements, weak passwords and a third party's monitoring credentials; the association declines to comment

The tracker DeXpose recorded on 2026-09-15 that SafePay had claimed an attack on ARA Lyss, the wastewater-treatment association at ara-lyss.ch, posting that the full leak would be published soon unless a company representative made contact (DeXpose, 2026-09-15). Inside IT reported on 2026-10-27 that SafePay has put the stolen data into the darknet, about 49 GB in the case of the Bernese association ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal, that the security firm Risikomonitor analysed it, and that the association's management declined to comment (Inside IT, 2026-10-27). Risikomonitor's analysis, relayed by Inside IT and not verified independently, finds about 3,200 e-mail addresses and data on more than 1,200 identifiable persons; user folders and a data store with content up to March 2026 that hold 255 password hits, 195 of them very weak; bank statements and a transaction list with more than 100 payments by private persons with name and address; the full login data to the monitoring portals of the photovoltaic plants of another company's customers, stored on the same server; and a 2015 applicant list with birth dates, civil status, former employer and interview notes that was never deleted (Inside IT, 2026-10-27).

BACS told Inside IT that SafePay, which relies on double extortion, is among the more active ransomware groups in Switzerland and, together with The Gentlemen, the third most active in 2026 after Akira and Payload, that it has no clear focus on Switzerland, and that it was first observed there in May 2025 (Inside IT, 2026-10-27). No source says how the attackers got in or that data was encrypted at the association.

Defender takeaway

item.content:encoded:
Update28 Oct 2026 03:52 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-intelactionsbodycvesevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27, fixing two unauthenticated read-side SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 (the sort-by parameter of store and category post lists) and CVE-2026-102789 (an editor task without a permission check), both scored CVSS 4.0 9.3 by the Joomla CNA and affecting every release up to 2.20.4.1. No exploitation is reported, Joomla 3 sites have no fix, and the action now points at 2.20.4.2.

Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27 with two security fixes rated Critical, for the versions 2.20.4.1 and earlier (Balbooa, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-102788 is in the sort-by URL parameter of store and category post lists and CVE-2026-102789 is a missing permission check on the editor task that loads blog posts (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27); Balbooa's fixes are a strict allowlist validation for the sort-by parameter and a user edit-level check on the editor task (Balbooa, 2026-10-27). mySites.guru says the sort value previously went into the ORDER BY part of the database query and reads the second flaw as a second anonymous route to the same query. mySites.guru reports that the Joomla CNA scores both CVSS 4.0 9.3 and lists every release from 1.0.0 to 2.20.4.1 as affected, and that only two PHP files differ between 2.20.4.1 and 2.20.4.2, one per fix (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27).

Both flaws read data: an anonymous visitor can extract the Joomla user table, with its password hashes, and every other table the site's extensions created. mySites.guru says about 95% of the Gridbox sites it monitors ran an affected version on the morning of the release, that sites on the Joomla 3 line stop at Gridbox 2.17.0.2, which has no fix for this year's flaws, and that there is no public report of exploitation yet (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27). Nothing here is reported exploited, unlike the July batches above; the version to be on is now 2.20.4.2.

Detection
In web access and database query logs, store or category list requests whose sort-by value is not one of the known sort keys, repeated anonymous calls to the Gridbox editor's blog-post task, and slow-query bursts from the web account; because the flaws only read, the post-patch check is credential hygiene on a site that was exposed, starting with administrator accounts nobody created, since the password hashes can be worked on offline.
Defender takeaway
Update to 2.20.4.2 now, communal and agency sites included, and move Joomla 3 sites to a supported Joomla (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27).

Open finding: CVE-2026-61425, Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: a client-supplied cookie is accepted as proof of identity, giving anonymous Super User access →

item.title: Update: Microsoft: Storm-0940 runs the ARTEX agent framework at machine speed; Expel adds an Okta self-registration technique

item.content:encoded:
Update27 Oct 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-10-27T0256Z-intelevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

Seoul police referred the leader of a criminal group to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for stealing 8.2 million records from more than 90 organizations, hospitals and universities among them, and extorting 38; BleepingComputer reports that the group used ARTEX, so the framework is now documented in criminal extortion use as well as in Storm-0940's state-aligned activity.

Seoul Metropolitan Police announced on 2026-10-26 that it referred a 32-year-old gang leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23, with six accomplices investigated without detention, for taking 8.2 million personal-data records and internal files from more than 90 organizations since September 2025, among them cram schools, hospitals, golf courses, universities and large-company affiliates, and for sending extortion e-mails (Yonhap, 2026-10-26, translated from Korean). BleepingComputer, citing local media, reports that the group demanded 360 million won (about USD 270,000) in 38 of the incidents in exchange for not leaking the data, that the police say the leader used the ARTEX framework, the same system used in the attacks on South Korean banks, and that he moved from conventional tools to AI utilities in late August 2026 (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-26). Yonhap counts 60 of the victims as hacked with AI and describes the system as the AI autonomous penetration-testing system used in the recent financial-sector data thefts without naming it, so the ARTEX name is BleepingComputer's (Yonhap, 2026-10-26). No encryption step is reported, and the police say AI lowered the barrier to entry and call this the first arrest in Korea in a large-scale hacking and personal-data theft case that exploited generative AI (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-26). The framework is therefore in use by a financially motivated criminal group as well as by the state-aligned actor Microsoft describes; no source reports a Swiss victim.

Open finding: ARTEX: Microsoft reports Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, running an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework against hundreds of organizations, with privileged cloud access in under three hours in some cases, and Expel sees the same infrastructure abuse Okta self-service registration →

item.title: Improvement: Fixed on 20 July, identified on 13 August, probed from 28 July: a CVE-keyed patch process never saw this one coming
item.description: Elastic Security Labs reproduced the chain and found that several public proofs of concept never trigger it, so a failed test does not show a host is patched; its process-lineage detection for the Swatchdog notification path is added to the detection guidance.
item.content:encoded:
Improvement24 Oct 2026 03:44 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_note

Elastic Security Labs reproduced the chain and found that several public proofs of concept never trigger it, so a failed test does not show a host is patched; its process-lineage detection for the Swatchdog notification path is added to the detection guidance.

Elastic Security Labs reproduced the exploit chain in its lab and describes it stage by stage: an SMTP client sends a recipient address with an unclosed angle bracket, Postfix logs it to /var/log/zimbra.log as an illegal-address warning, Zimbra's bundled Swatchdog daemon matches a log line of the form "Service status change: <host> <service> changed from stopped to running", and the notification routine places the service field into a Perl backtick string that /bin/sh runs, giving code execution as the zimbra user, who can read every mailbox and send as any local identity (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23). Its practical finding is that several public proofs of concept write a payload that Swatchdog never matches, so a failed test looks like a patched server; Elastic's own proof of concept proves execution with an out-of-band callback that changes nothing on disk, and it says upgrading to 10.1.20 or later is the only complete fix (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23).

Its detection is a process sequence on one host within 30 seconds, a shell started by the Perl Swatchdog script with snmptrap in its command line followed by any child of that shell other than snmptrap; on a healthy host the notification shell starts only snmptrap, so any other child is the discriminator (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23). Where exploitation is found, Elastic lists standard indicators of remote code execution, phishing mail originating from the server, compromise of local databases, signing keys and LDAP exports, and less direct surfaces beyond the mail store (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23).

Open finding: CVE-2026-73570, Zimbra Collaboration: a pre-auth command injection patched without a CVE in July is exploited, with probing before disclosure and root escalation, secret theft and cluster-wide movement observed →

item.content:encoded:
Update24 Oct 2026 03:41 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelactionsbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

The Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says in a letter of 2026-10-23 that data of about 1,800 of its insured persons (about 1,700 who left in 2024 and 2025, with exit-benefit amounts and IBANs, and about 80 on disability pensions) sat on the attacked supplier server for two ongoing projects; it has no certain evidence the data were taken but finds it plausible, and it writes to all insured because it cannot exclude more.

The Ticino cantonal pension fund IPCT has put numbers on its exposure in a letter of 2026-10-23 to its roughly 17,000 active insured and 10,000 pensioners (IPCT, 2026-10-23). PK Softech told it in the late afternoon of 2026-10-14 that the authorities had established that personal data were taken from the supplier's servers, without saying which funds the data belonged to, and the fund's checks to date found among the documents on the attacked server data of about 1,800 persons, held there for two ongoing projects of spot checks and recalculations (IPCT, 2026-10-23). About 1,700 are persons who left the fund through resignation or death in 2024 and 2025: surname, first name, postal address, date of birth, AHV number and insured number, the exit-benefit amount and the receiving fund with its bank account (IBAN), and the personal IBAN for about 50 who were paid out directly, with no e-mail address or telephone number (IPCT, 2026-10-23). About 80 are insured persons on a disability pension whose passive pension data was being updated: name, date of birth, AHV number, insured number, passive insured salary, passive retirement assets, degree and start of invalidity, with no contact data (IPCT, 2026-10-23).

The fund says it has no certain evidence that these data were taken but that it appears plausible, that savings capital and pensions of all insured are untouched, that the cantonal administration's IT centre hosting the fund's infrastructure was not breached, and that it filed a criminal complaint against unknown persons and was recognised as private plaintiff, while the Federal Prosecutor's Office and the federal police investigate (IPCT, 2026-10-23; Ticinonline, 2026-10-23). It decided to send the letter to all insured because its information is partial, the analyses are still evolving and it may never have certainty, and it asks them to watch for unexpected e-mails, calls and messages over the coming weeks and never to disclose passwords, access data or personal data unless sure of the requester (IPCT, 2026-10-23). The letter names PK Softech's other customers as Publica, large cantonal public funds such as Bern and Zurich and company funds such as Migros and Post, for hundreds of thousands of insured persons in total (IPCT, 2026-10-23).

item.title: Update: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
item.description: The supplier's written pledge to delete Publica's 2019 migration data was apparently not kept, Inside IT relays that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira exfiltrated data, though that is second-hand and neither the Confederation nor Publica has itself named the actor, and the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says all its insured could potentially be involved but has no evidence yet that data was taken.
item.content:encoded:
Update23 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-23T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

The supplier's written pledge to delete Publica's 2019 migration data was apparently not kept, Inside IT relays that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira exfiltrated data, though that is second-hand and neither the Confederation nor Publica has itself named the actor, and the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says all its insured could potentially be involved but has no evidence yet that data was taken.

Tamedia's Tages-Anzeiger reported on 2026-10-21 that PK Softech AG had confirmed in writing to Publica that it deleted the data, and that this apparently did not happen: its summary says the company reported in January that it had deleted the information on former Federal Councillors and agents, "but this was false" (translated from German; Tages-Anzeiger, 2026-10-21); the article is paywalled. Inside IT, working from the Tamedia research, dates the written confirmation to January 2026 and says PK Softech confirmed it held no personal data in plaintext and had deleted the data of the 2019 migration, that Publica confirmed the sequence (after the Xplain case it asked the supplier to delete all legacy data, including that of the 2019 migration, and received written confirmation), that Publica is clarifying why personal data presumably lay on the servers regardless, and that PK Softech did not answer and does not comment on individual customer relationships (Inside IT, 2026-10-22). 20 Minuten reports the same sequence and notes that PK Softech received the data in 2019 in a migration for Publica (20 Minuten, 2026-10-22).

Inside IT also relays, from Tamedia, that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed that data was extracted by the Akira ransomware group, which still threatens to publish or sell it; 20 Minuten writes that according to findings so far Akira stole the data (Inside IT, 2026-10-22; 20 Minuten, 2026-10-22). This is a reported confirmation of the actor by an authority, but it reaches the reader second-hand through the paywalled Tamedia article: the Federal Prosecutor's Office is not quoted directly, and Publica's own page, in its entry of 2026-10-20, still says it is clarifying whether data of Publica left and whose (Publica, 2026-10-20).

The Ticino cantonal pension fund IPCT says through Corriere del Ticino, relayed by Ticinonline on 2026-10-20, that potentially all of its insured could be involved but that there is no evidence yet that their data was actually taken; it has filed a complaint with the Federal Prosecutor's Office and is preparing a letter to the insured warning of telephone and e-mail fraud (Ticinonline, 2026-10-20). TicinoNews adds, from its own information, that a folder labelled IPCT with the data of a few hundred insured persons was on the supplier's server, while IPCT, which has about 27,000 affiliated persons, says it has no certainty yet that data of its insured is involved (TicinoNews, 2026-10-21).

item.title: Kaspersky: a UEFI bootkit ran on fully patched Windows because Microsoft's Secure Boot revocation is off by default
item.description: Kaspersky GReAT reports BlackX, a UEFI bootkit similar to BlackLotus that exploits Baton Drop (CVE-2022-21894) to enrol attacker keys and load a kernel driver that blinds security products, installed after attackers held administrator rights on networks of diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan; Kaspersky attributes it to APT41 with medium confidence. The targeted machines were fully patched, because Microsoft's fix revokes the old boot-manager certificate only when an administrator sets a registry flag and runs a scheduled task.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2022-21894 +1exploitedNATOB2

BlackX: Kaspersky finds a BlackLotus-style UEFI bootkit on fully patched Windows machines of Central Asian diplomatic bodies, because the Baton Drop fix does not revoke the old boot-manager certificate until an administrator triggers it

Kaspersky GReAT reports that in early 2026 it found BlackX, a UEFI bootkit similar to BlackLotus, used against diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan after the attackers held administrator privileges: an installer takes an RC4-encrypted package and its key as command-line arguments and drops files to the system and UEFI partitions that exploit Baton Drop (CVE-2022-21894) to enrol attacker-controlled Machine Owner Keys, so arbitrary EFI files load despite Secure Boot (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22). Kaspersky ties the exploitation to Baton Drop alone; CVE-2023-24932, the flaw Microsoft's revocation guidance is titled for, appears in its post only as the one a UEFI component in ESET's FishMonger report might exploit (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22). The bootkit injects a kernel driver, signed with a certificate its issuer has since revoked, that disables process, thread and registry callbacks and ETW providers of security products; the user-mode payloads were a RAT that uses Google Drive, OneDrive or Yandex.Disk for command and control and a sideloaded loader (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22).

The targeted machines were fully patched. Microsoft's fix revokes the Windows Production PCA 2011 certificate only when an administrator sets a Secure Boot registry flag and runs the Secure-Boot-Update scheduled task (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22); Microsoft's own article says the mitigations in the updates of 2024-07-09 and later are not enabled by default and the Enforcement Phase date is still to be announced (Microsoft Support, 2026-09-30), and Kaspersky says that phase has not been implemented and the certificate's expiry on 2026-10-19 does not stop the vulnerable binaries loading unless it is on the forbidden list (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22). Kaspersky attributes the campaign to APT41 with medium confidence, resting on the identifier "xdd" shared with a kernel implant in ESET's June 2026 FishMonger report, DLL sideloading and OLLVM (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Any Windows device that boots with Secure Boot, has the updates of 2024-07-09 or later and has not had the revocation steps applied; Microsoft's check is that the forbidden-list (DBX) variable contains Microsoft Windows Production PCA 2011, which a PowerShell test returns as True once the revocation is in (Microsoft Support, 2026-09-30).
Detection
The installer needs administrator rights, so the hunt starts with the administrator-level intrusion that precedes it; the behaviors Kaspersky describes are process creation of an executable from a program-data subfolder that takes an encrypted data file and a key as arguments, file writes to the EFI system partition by processes that are not servicing, kernel driver loads signed by an unfamiliar or revoked certificate, a signed executable renamed to look like an updater that loads a sideloaded DLL, and non-browser processes talking to consumer cloud storage (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22). Because the driver disables security-product callbacks and ETW providers, quiet host telemetry after a reboot on a machine that ran the installer is not evidence that nothing ran, although Kaspersky found that the driver's tampering routines, written for Kaspersky and Avast products, failed to interfere with Kaspersky products (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22).
Defender takeaway
A patched Windows fleet is not protected against this class until the revocation is applied, so decide which devices get Microsoft's procedure and in what order; Microsoft warns that the revocation cannot be reverted while Secure Boot is in use, that BitLocker recovery keys should be backed up first, and that recovery and install media must be updated (Microsoft Support, 2026-09-30).

item.title: Microsoft: Storm-0940 runs the ARTEX agent framework at machine speed; Expel adds an Okta self-registration technique
item.description: Microsoft reports that since at least September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, has used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth-application abuse against hundreds of organizations across many industries including government, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in several cases. Expel independently saw the same infrastructure create its own accounts through Okta self-service registration, enrol Okta Verify and sign in to applications, and CrowdStrike and Recorded Future document another actor using the same framework. Seoul police referred a criminal group's leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for extorting 38 of more than 90 organizations, hospitals and universities among them, with the same framework according to BleepingComputer.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

ARTEX: Microsoft reports Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, running an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework against hundreds of organizations, with privileged cloud access in under three hours in some cases, and Expel sees the same infrastructure abuse Okta self-service registration

Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports that as early as September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor active since 2021, used the agentic penetration-testing framework ARTEX to automate attacks on hundreds of organizations across many industries, government and military among them (Microsoft, 2026-10-21). ARTEX is an open-source multi-agent LLM system that can use any AI model and runs a penetration test from reconnaissance to exfiltration with little human involvement (Microsoft, 2026-10-21). Microsoft says ARTEX accelerated the abuse of compromised applications already granted access to Microsoft 365 tenants (Microsoft, 2026-10-21), and Expel adds that it is not a vulnerability and only speeds up familiar techniques such as password spraying and OAuth-application abuse (Expel, 2026-10-21); most targeting failed, yet several cases went from first targeting to privileged cloud access in under three hours (Microsoft, 2026-10-21). Microsoft assesses the same actor was behind the ConnectWise Cloud Backup application-credential abuse (Microsoft, 2026-10-21).

Expel saw Storm-0940 infrastructure scan a customer and, from 2026-10-13, abuse its Okta self-service registration with no ConnectWise application involved: the attacker created five accounts of its own, enrolled Okta Verify on three of them about a minute after activation, made 50 single sign-on logins with more than 100 OAuth tokens issued and ran a password spray that Okta ThreatInsight blocked (Expel, 2026-10-21). Expel says the shared source address is its only link to Storm-0940, the activity alone does not prove ARTEX was used, and it had not seen the technique reported before (Expel, 2026-10-21). Other actors use it: CrowdStrike analysed an unnamed, probably Chinese-speaking and financially motivated actor that ran ARTEX against South Korean financial institutions from late September (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-07), and Recorded Future, which tracks that activity as TAG-217, says use of ARTEX and other AI penetration-testing tools is not limited to it (Recorded Future, 2026-10-16).

Wiz Research independently reports that throughout October 2026 it tracked an actor using ARTEX-associated tooling, overlapping with Storm-0940, against IT and software vendors, focused on identity providers (Okta, Entra, Cognito) and Microsoft 365 integrations, and says that most attempts failed and that none of the techniques is novel (Wiz, 2026-10-22). It describes a consistent sequence: downloading JavaScript bundles, exposed source maps, runtime configuration and OpenAPI documents, then calling internal API routes by name minutes later; fabricated authorization codes and malformed state values against Microsoft OAuth callbacks; unsigned JWTs tried against more than 60 SSO route variants in two minutes; and account-recovery, sign-up and Cognito calls such as InitiateAuth, ForgotPassword and ResendConfirmationCode (Wiz, 2026-10-22). Its password sprays against Entra and Okta hit hundreds of users, mainly software engineers, in bursts of 20 to 60 minutes with a unique user agent per burst, a median gap of one second between attempts and new source addresses within minutes of a block (Wiz, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Any tenant that relies on password sign-in or grants OAuth consent to applications, and any Okta org with self-service registration enabled; not using ConnectWise does not exclude exposure (Expel, 2026-10-21).
Detection
In the authentication logs of every identity provider in use, bursts of failed logons and lockouts spread over many accounts; in the Okta system log, newly self-registered accounts that enrol Okta Verify and start single sign-on within minutes; and in the Entra audit log, credentials or certificates added to applications that nobody on your team created and any application that assigns itself a directory role (Microsoft, 2026-10-21; Expel, 2026-10-21). A clean audit log is not proof of no access, because Microsoft Graph directory reads leave no Entra audit record (Expel, 2026-10-21). In web access logs of an application exposed to the same actor, Wiz points to source-map and OpenAPI downloads followed minutes later by calls to internal routes that appear only in those files, and to sign-in telemetry showing a new user agent for each burst of attempts at a one-second cadence (Wiz, 2026-10-22).

Triage: Python and curl user agents match common legitimate automation, so Expel treats them as supporting evidence only, and a Python user agent on an application that normally calls Microsoft Graph with a .NET SDK is the anomaly (Expel, 2026-10-21).

Defender takeaway
Expel's reading is that the framework adds speed, not a new vulnerability, so the levers are the identity controls it runs into: least privilege on multi-tenant application permissions and consent grants, alerting on credential additions and privileged role assignments by applications, and a review of self-registered Okta accounts since 2026-10-13 (Microsoft, 2026-10-21; Expel, 2026-10-21).
Improvement24 Oct 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_note

Wiz Research reports an actor using ARTEX-associated tooling, overlapping with Storm-0940, against IT and software vendors throughout October 2026, focused on Okta, Entra and Cognito and on Microsoft 365 integrations, with most attempts failing (Wiz, 2026-10-22). It describes the log signatures of the agent: source-map and OpenAPI downloads followed minutes later by calls to internal routes that appear only in those files, fabricated OAuth callback values, unsigned JWTs tried against more than 60 SSO route variants in two minutes, account-recovery and sign-up calls, and password-spray bursts of 20 to 60 minutes against Entra and Okta with a unique user agent per burst and a median gap of one second between attempts (Wiz, 2026-10-22). Wiz says chaining, automatic adaptation to rate limits and blocks, and tests against heavily scrutinised Microsoft OAuth flows separate the agent from a human operator (Wiz, 2026-10-22).

Update27 Oct 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-10-27T0256Z-intelevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

Seoul Metropolitan Police announced on 2026-10-26 that it referred a 32-year-old gang leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23, with six accomplices investigated without detention, for taking 8.2 million personal-data records and internal files from more than 90 organizations since September 2025, among them cram schools, hospitals, golf courses, universities and large-company affiliates, and for sending extortion e-mails (Yonhap, 2026-10-26, translated from Korean). BleepingComputer, citing local media, reports that the group demanded 360 million won (about USD 270,000) in 38 of the incidents in exchange for not leaking the data, that the police say the leader used the ARTEX framework, the same system used in the attacks on South Korean banks, and that he moved from conventional tools to AI utilities in late August 2026 (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-26). Yonhap counts 60 of the victims as hacked with AI and describes the system as the AI autonomous penetration-testing system used in the recent financial-sector data thefts without naming it, so the ARTEX name is BleepingComputer's (Yonhap, 2026-10-26). No encryption step is reported, and the police say AI lowered the barrier to entry and call this the first arrest in Korea in a large-scale hacking and personal-data theft case that exploited generative AI (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-26). The framework is therefore in use by a financially motivated criminal group as well as by the state-aligned actor Microsoft describes; no source reports a Swiss victim.

CISA said there was no indication that sensitive data was compromised and that it was adding safeguards; the staffing loss of nearly a third of its workforce is Krebs's context, not a CISA statement about contractor oversight. LZ-DSO, which appears to stand for Landing Zone DevSecOps, the agency's secure code development environment, was one of the dozens of internal systems whose passwords sat in the exposed CSV; the plaintext credentials to CISA's internal Artifactory package repository were a separate item in the archive (Krebs on Security, 2026-05-18). item.title: Correction: SzafirHost before 1.2.1 can load a malicious class from a JAR that passes its signature check (CVE-2026-44088)
item.description: Polish qualified electronic signatures are not recognised as equivalent in Switzerland, which has no mutual recognition agreement with the EU, so the flaw carries no Swiss signature-trust exposure. CERT Polska states only that combining a genuine signed JAR with a malicious ZIP can lead to remote code execution in SzafirHost before 1.2.1, and names neither a download-path attack nor silent signing of fraudulent documents nor the public-sector workflows that rely on it. item.content:encoded:
Correction21 Oct 2026 20:21 UTCrun 2026-10-21T1148Z-auditactionsaffected_productsbodyclassificationcvesevidenceheadlineprioritysectorssourcessourcing_notesummarytechniquestitleverification

Polish qualified electronic signatures are not recognised as equivalent in Switzerland, which has no mutual recognition agreement with the EU, so the flaw carries no Swiss signature-trust exposure. CERT Polska states only that combining a genuine signed JAR with a malicious ZIP can lead to remote code execution in SzafirHost before 1.2.1, and names neither a download-path attack nor silent signing of fraudulent documents nor the public-sector workflows that rely on it. The CVSS 4.0 score of 8.6 is CERT-PL's as carried by ENISA's EUVD.

Switzerland does not recognise Polish qualified signatures under an eIDAS-equivalent framework: no mutual recognition agreement exists between Switzerland and the EU, and without one a foreign qualified signature is not equivalent to a qualified signature under Swiss law (BAKOM).
